title: Why the f is there no server where you don't lose your ship when you die?

posts.cooked:
The current setup is dumb as f.

Yes it worked 15 years ago. Now it's ran by whales who play 10-20 multiboxed accounts.
Out of 30.000 players online, there are probably 5000-10000 real humans playing.

It's extremely hostile to new players and people inevitably quit.

Rule number 8
If you lose stuff, it's almost always your fault. Really, only yours.

You dont need to "win" against multiboxer gankers to have fun. You just need to learn how to avoid them and never give them a chance to get you but not everybody has the brains to do that,

I mean... New player ships don't cost anything. Hell you can get infinite free frigates from the SoE.

Losing them in the early game doesn't mean anything but your ship's value wouldn't mean much either if it wasn't an asset that could disappear and need replacing.

Well you don't lose your ship when you die; you lose your clone.

You lose your ship when it gets destroyed, and it would be a bit tricky to have something be destroyed yet also not destroyed.

What would be nice is a ship cloning feature like for the player clones. Just an instant, or nearly so, buyback so you don't need to fly all over to get all the equipment and stuff.

It wouldn't be such a pain to lose a ship if outfitting was such a mission, if of course you have the ISK

what kind of ships are you even losing anyway? probably worth peanuts so whats the deal just buy another one lol, if you are gonna go fight a war where you expect losses then you field cheap ships that you can replace, obvious stuff tbh

drop the ego buddy its just a ship dont worry about it

You would think that, as many times as the "pve only" pops up, that CCP would try and do something about it. Exordium was a good start and proves that Eve COULD have a pve only server. However, after trying Eve out every 5 years, and keeping tabs on its progress I have realized that it will never happen. Eve is meant to be a pvp game - period.
To me this is ironic. It is gankers that keep this game afloat. Almost all the gankers that I have seen, on all the games that I have played, over many years, are not pvp players. They do not want to fight a one-on-one battle, they want to dominate and humiliate their targets. They are bullies, not fighters. Eve is not so much a pvp game as a gankers paradise.
Still, Eve is a a GREAT game. Though, due to its complexity, it will never have a huge audience, it could have a much bigger audience if it offered a pve only server. I say this because topics like this, "why no pve server", pop up ALL the time, and are heard in rookie chat every day, year after year. I wish Eve Online the best but, my visiting time, as a pve player, is over.

The funny thing about the PvE conversation is it really makes no sense once you start actually thinking about it. And this comes from a mainly solo/PvE player.

The whole concept of system security ratings would be pointless then as the NPCs only show up in specific areas. So in theory all areas will be 1.0 security. Unless of course the idea is to make all 0.5 and above like 1.0 and lower areas are lawless or limited Concord response as it is now.

I do understand the frustration though. It's not fun losing millions or even billions of ISK, but that is the game. You either accept it or if you don't, then this is one of those cases where the game is not for you.
I just lost my Vexor (around 30 mil I think), although not from PvP, damn Abyssal time limits, first major ship loss after starting again, and it's not fun at all. But you have to accept that it will happen. Definitely not easy though and it takes away a lot of the fun.
To me though the money loss is not even the worse part. It's buying and fitting a new ship. Wish Amazon existed in game and you can order everything online and get it delivered (yes you can partly do that, but not get all the modules and ship delivered to your home station on a rebuy)

The beauty of this game though is even with the losses, it still makes us want to play it because it's so awesome.
Rule #1, never undock. Ever. Just ship spin. This is the way.
If you want no repercussions for dying then Star Trek Online is still kicking and, as a fan of the franchise, has some meaningfully great story beats.
